findings.message: The repo-name derivation is now written twice, and the two copies can disagree. The new copy is at entrypoint.sh:18-19: strip every trailing '/', strip any-case '.git', then take '##*/'. The existing copy is `azdo_repo` in plugins/specclaw-sync/lib/azdo.sh:46-48: `name="${url##*/_git/}"; name="${name%%/*}"; name="${name%.git}"`. That one strips only lowercase '.git'. The round-11/final-pass fix ("any-case .git") patched only the fleet copy. Inside the pod, AZDO_REPO is preset, so the azdo.sh copy is skipped. Outside the pod, specclaw-azdo-pr and the other sync tools still use it. Extract one shared parser and use it at both call sites, or apply the same normalisation in azdo.sh. Then add the `.GIT` and trailing-'//' rows to the sync tests.
findings.scenario: The remote URL is https://dev.azure.com/o/p/_git/R.GIT. The fleet pod sets AZDO_REPO=R. A local `specclaw-azdo-pr` run against the same remote resolves the repo as `R.GIT`. One project gets two different repository names, and the ADO repositories/R.GIT API lookup fails.

findings.message: The script runs under `set -euo pipefail`. `repo_name="$FLEET_REPO_URL"` dereferences the variable unguarded, so an unset FLEET_REPO_URL aborts the entrypoint before `finish` writes $STATUS/exit. The WARN on line 20 uses `${FLEET_REPO_URL:-}`, so it seems meant to handle the missing case, but it is only reachable when the variable is set and empty. The new test row `|none|WARN` covers only the empty-string case. Use `${FLEET_REPO_URL:-}` on line 18 too, or fail through `finish` with a clear status.

The WARN line echoes the raw FLEET_REPO_URL into the pod log. If a dispatcher ever passes a URL that carries userinfo, such as https://user:token@host/, the token lands in the logs. Elsewhere the image takes care to keep tokens out of the clone URL and git args. Log a redacted form (strip `*@`) or omit the URL.
